A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ShowHowTo and provide readable main text, figures, tables, mathematical notation, and complete Appendices A–F. The method, experiments, and relocated material can be reliably matched across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation experiments, training ablations, a user study, dataset-validation results, FID scores, and downstream classification results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds WikiHow evaluation, a keyframe-selection user study, and performance breakdowns by sequence length and task category.

M1.justification: The automatic dataset pipeline and DynamiCrafter-based generation method remain unchanged, including temporal frame alignment, per-frame text conditioning, input-image conditioning, and variable-length training. Additional explanations do not establish a procedural or architectural change.

E1.justification: Section 5.1 adds zero-shot evaluation on 1,442 non-illustrated WikiHow-VGSI sequences, extending evaluation to an external photographic instruction source. WikiHow already appeared in the training-data ablation. Existing ShowHowTo and GenHowTo evaluations remain; the new category breakdown uses existing task coverage.

E2.justification: The generation comparator sets remain unchanged, including their extension to WikiHow. Appendix A adds manual keyframe selection as a human reference comparator against automatic DFN-CLIP selection in a blinded preference study.

E3.justification: New evaluation protocols include randomly selecting 1,442 photographic WikiHow sequences and reporting Step Faithfulness and Scene Consistency, plus a blinded comparison of manual and automatic keyframes for 100 steps with ties reported. Existing training settings, ShowHowTo test split, and core metric definitions remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained training ablations, v2 adds direct human assessment of keyframe-selection quality in Appendix A and diagnostic analyses by generated sequence length and task category in Appendix E, Tables 8–9. These substantially expand analysis of dataset quality and performance variation; generated-length analysis is distinct from the existing training-length ablation.

E5.justification: Dataset dispersion summaries and the metric–human-preference correlation analysis remain unchanged. v2 adds no seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures. The new study's sample size and preference percentages concern evaluation design and results.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds WikiHow results: ShowHowTo scores 0.72/0.12 on Step/Scene, while AURORA scores 0.33/0.15. Tables 8–9 add length/category results, and Appendix A reports 18% preference for automatic keyframes, 36% for manual selection, and 46% ties. Retained benchmark and ablation scores are unchanged; Table 1 drops its Overall entries.

T1.justification: The mathematical problem formulation, sequence notation, and methodological reasoning remain unchanged. Neither version introduces theoretical results or proofs that are added, removed, or revised in the other.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: automatic construction of the large instructional dataset, scene-conditioned visual instruction generation, and strong performance across the three evaluation dimensions. The additional evidence does not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: v2 explains why generated images can exceed source images on CLIP-based faithfulness, interprets category differences through training prevalence and retrieval ambiguity, and discusses length-related degradation. The training-data discussion emphasizes extraction quality on shared source videos. Existing object-state and rare-object limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 points readers to the project website for the selected WikiHow sequence list and explicitly states that comparison methods are evaluated without fine-tuning. These add reproducibility information; Appendix C's hardware, optimization, training budget, sampling settings, and code/model access statements remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix A newly contrasts narration-based step extraction with GenHowTo's frame-based captioning and argues that the latter produces insufficiently detailed captions. The cited-work set and broader research positioning remain unchanged; the reference-year correction is bibliographic.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording corrections, tightens paragraphs, adds explanatory passages and cross-references, and retitles the GenHowTo evaluation discussion. The main section organization and Appendix A–F structure are retained.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains dataset-grouped columns and loses Overall; Tables 8–9 are added. Tables 2–4 rename Overall to Average, Table 7's heading/caption changes, and Figure 12 moves from page 14 to page 15. Existing illustrations are retained, with limited layout reflow.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens external validation and diagnostic transparency through the WikiHow evaluation, direct keyframe-quality assessment, and length/category breakdowns. These provide useful incremental evidence while retaining the method and existing results. The new evidence also exposes limits: WikiHow scene consistency trails AURORA, 0.12 versus 0.15, so it supports a modest quality improvement without establishing uniformly superior performance.
